newsitem.title: USA: Viper militiamen sentenced to prison in Arizona.
newsitem.headline: Viper militiamen sentenced to prison in Arizona.

text.p: Three members of the self-styled Viper Militia, arrested in a series of raids by anti-terrorist agents last year, were sentenced Wednesday to jail terms for conspiracy to make bombs.

At the time of their arrest last July, President Clinton said "a terrible terrorist attack" had been averted, but prosecutors later said there was no indication the suspects were planning any specific attacks.
Defence lawyers characterised the suspects as gun enthusiasts who went to remote desert areas of Arizona to "blow up dirt."

Videotapes seized at the time of their arrests and later shown in court depicted several members firing guns and setting off explosions in remote areas. Agents also seized manuals on bomb-making and maps pointing out federal and state buildings in the Phoenix area.

Some of those arrested also were in possession of machine guns and quantities of ammonium nitrate -- a chemical common in fertilisers. The chemical can be used to manufacture explosives and was a component of the deadly bomb that devastated a federal building in Oklahoma City in 1995.
The three sentenced Wednesday had all pleaded guilty in an agreement with federal prosecutors. Ten of their fellow paramilitary militia members were to be sentenced later.
Two more Viper militiamen have pleaded not guilty and their trial is set to start March 25.

The three sentenced by Federal Judge Earl Carroll in Phoenix Wednesday were Henry Overturf, Walter Sanville and Scott Shero. All three were convicted of one count of conspiracy to manufacture and possess destructive devices.
Sanville, 37, was also convicted on two counts of unlawful possession of machine guns. He was jailed for 37 months and fined $2,800.
Overturf, 37, was jailed for 12 months and one day and fined $1,600, while Shero, 31, received a 24-month prison term and a $1,600 fine. All three were also put on 36 months probation.
All three apologised to the government and their families. "I never intended on hurting anybody or causing any damage," said Shero.
